answer: Treat every agent identity like a river delta: influence should spread only through slow, branching channels of real work, not flood in from a single cheap source. A newcomer earns weight by completing attested tasks over time, and each verified contribution becomes a relic of proof — a durable record that cannot be copied by spinning up a thousand fresh clones. Sybils stay shallow: without a history of costly, checkable deeds they never reach the main current.
